title: SQL Injection via ADO.NET String Interpolation
platform_conditions: .NET Framework 4.x and modern .NET with ADO.NET providers (SqlClient, Npgsql, MySqlConnector, Microsoft.Data.Sqlite)
security_mechanism: The ADO.NET parameter mechanism (SqlParameterCollection) ships values to the server out-of-band so they can never alter statement structure. C# string interpolation ($"...", concatenation, string.Format) composes the user value into CommandText before the provider parses it, so a single quote or SQL token inside the value is interpreted as statement syntax. The same flaw reaches raw-SQL helpers of ORMs and any SqlCommand built from an interpolated string, including stored-procedure invocation through Exec/EXECUTE composed at runtime.

source_sink_clues.source: Request route/query/body fields, filter and sort names from the client, and any value concatenated into CommandText.
source_sink_clues.sink: SqlCommand / NpgsqlCommand.CommandText (or the provider's raw-SQL API) assigned from an interpolated or concatenated string, then ExecuteReader/ExecuteNonQuery/ExecuteScalar

tracking_guards: Verify every dynamic value travels as a SqlParameter with @name placeholders in the text (AddWithValue or explicit SqlParameter objects); for identifiers that cannot be parameterized (column names, sort direction) require an allowlist dictionary mapping client keys to fixed SQL fragments rather than quoting the client string.
not_candidate_when: All values bind through SqlParameter objects, the only interpolated fragments come from a fixed server-side mapping (never raw client text), or the CommandText is a compile-time constant with parameters.
synthetic_vulnerable_example: SqlCommand cmd = new SqlCommand($"SELECT * FROM Users WHERE Name = '{name}'");
synthetic_safe_example: SqlCommand cmd = new SqlCommand("SELECT * FROM Users WHERE Name = @name"); cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@name", name);
public_references: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html
OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
